commit.message:
Give django-mfa2 the primary key type its migrations create (#1266)

Settings set DEFAULT_AUTO_FIELD to BigAutoField, and django-mfa2's
AppConfig names no default_auto_field, so Django reads mfa's models
with big ids while its shipped migrations create regular ones. Every
migrate prints that mfa has model changes no migration covers, and an
unscoped makemigrations --check fails.

That check is the one setup_templates.sh runs during build.sh. When
it fails, the script generates and applies migrations on the spot, so
deploys wrote an mfa migration into the build machine's installed
package (one generated on Oct 8 was still there). CI's ci_setup_db.sh
does the same on every run, so its test database differed from prod's.

INSTALLED_APPS now loads mfa through a subclass of its AppConfig that
pins AutoField, which matches the migrations. No schema change. A new
test runs the unscoped check, so a third-party app's drift fails in CI
instead of being papered over at deploy time.
